Taking a new client front to back

From an empty screen to a signed pack and a recorded payment, across both SAT-C applications.

Written by walking it, 5 September 2026 · every screen below was driven in a real browser and photographed as it appeared · the client, the figures and the documents are invented — no real client data appears anywhere in this document.

Read this once before you start. Each step is one action. Under each one, Correct tells you what the screen should look like, so you can tell when something has gone wrong. Where a step carries a Careful note, that is a fault in the software as it stands today — the note tells you how to work around it, not how to fix it.

THE ROUTE

Part A — The desk — satc_system

1Start the desk app

DoDouble-click SATC.bat in satc_system\. It opens your browser at http://127.0.0.1:5050. Leave the black window open — closing it stops the app.

CorrectA left-hand menu of seventeen items, and the page title Dashboard. If the port is busy the app picks another one and prints it — read the address in the black window rather than assuming 5050.

2Check the machine is ready

DoClick Setup at the bottom of the menu.

CorrectSeven rows, every one with a green tick. Data store shows the folder your practice data lives in — read it, and make sure it is the one you meant. Cloud vision should read OFF — documents never leave this machine.

3Clear the demo data — once, on a new install

DoStill on Setup, click Clear sample data & start clean. Your browser asks you to confirm; click OK. This cannot be undone.

CorrectThe cream banner across the top disappears, and so does the Sample data panel.

CarefulDo this before you add your first real client, not after. The banner comes back once a client exists (a known fault), and the button that clears it would then delete that client.

4Create the client

DoClick Clients, then + New client (or Engagements → + New client). Choose Person or Business, type the first and last name, and click Create client. SSN, email and phone are optional.

CorrectA page headed <name> is set up — how do you want to start? with three cards, and a reference like SATC-001000 under the name.

CarefulThe SSN box accepts anything at all — it does not check the format. Type it carefully.

5Choose how you are taking them in

DoClick Start interview → on the middle card, then pick the workflow that matches the job — for a personal return that is Personal 1040 core. Click Start →.

CorrectThe client's name and reference at the top, and only the workflows that suit that kind of client.

6Run the interview

DoChoose New client or Returning client, set the Filing status, then work down the thirteen questions. Fill in Due date and Tax year at the bottom and click Generate checklist.

CorrectYou land on the engagement, showing the workflow, tax year, due date and a scoreboard.

CarefulEvery question starts on “No”. Nothing marks a question as unasked, and the internal checklist prints those defaults as the client's own answers — including the three risk questions (marketplace insurance, digital assets, foreign accounts). Touch every row deliberately.

7Record the engagement reference

DoIn the Engagement ref box type the number from the client's own paperwork — the format is YYYY-NNNN, e.g. 2026-0001 — and click Record ref.

CorrectRecorded. Clearing the box and saving removes it. Anything that is not YYYY-NNNN is refused by name, and a good reference already on file is not disturbed by a failed attempt.

CarefulThis is the join between the letters the client holds and this system's own key. Until it is set, an arriving document cannot be matched to this client.

8Send the document request

DoOn the engagement, click View email text to read the request, or Print client list for a paper copy. ✉ Email request (Outlook draft) opens a draft — it does not send.

CorrectThe requests grouped under headings (Core documents, Prior year, Investments), each with a suggested-by date.

9Track what has come back

DoClick Documents. Click Received when something arrives. To close a request that will never arrive, type the reason in the box and click N/A.

CorrectThe row turns satisfied or n/a and the red badge on the menu counts down. N/A without a reason is refused — “a bare N/A is indistinguishable from never having asked.”

CarefulReceived closes the request but does not write anything into the Arrived register below it — the one the screen says a regulation requires. Keep your own note of how and when a document reached you.

10Read a folder of the client's documents

DoClick Intake, type or paste the full path to the folder, and click Scan folder. Check the list, then click Read & stage these N documents →.

CorrectEach file with its detected type, how it was identified (text is a real read; filename is a guess) and a confidence badge.

CarefulTwo faults live on this screen. If the folder does not exist you get either a confident list of somebody else's six demo documents, or nothing at all — never “that folder is not there.” Check the path character by character. And everything you post from here goes to client SATC-001000 and tax year 2024, whoever you meant. Until that is fixed, use this screen only when SATC-001000 is the client you want.

11Confirm what was read

DoClick Staging. Check each value against the document on the right — View source ↗ opens it. Correct anything wrong and click Save on that row; Confirm accepts a flagged one; Delete removes a stray.

CorrectEvery row shows a confidence, a status, and who put it there — system:intake for a machine read, human:owner once you touch it.

CarefulA money box accepts any text at all, and if what you type is not a number the workpaper silently keeps the machine's original figure while the screen goes on showing yours as confirmed. After correcting a figure, check it on the client page.

12Post the confirmed values

DoClick Post N confirmed → workpaper & data mart.

CorrectYou land on the client, with Just posted N confirmed values to the data mart and a Workpaper inputs table showing each amount and the document it came from.

CarefulThe number posted is smaller than the number on the button because two W-2s add into one 1040 line. That is correct; the screen just does not say so.

13Raise the invoice

DoClick Invoices → Raise an invoice. Pick the client and tax year. If the client is on a reduced rate, choose it, type the reason in Why this client is on that plan, and click Set. Then pick the service, quantity, and click Add to the invoice.

CorrectA What the client will see block: full value, the named reduction, and the total due.

CarefulThe red line saying “No rate plan agreed … the practice default 'standard' applies” does not update when you set a plan. Trust the totals at the bottom, not that sentence. A reduced rate with no reason is silently ignored — check the totals to see whether it took.

14Issue it

DoSet the issue date and the payment terms, then click Issue invoice.

CorrectThe invoice gets its number, and the page says it cannot be edited — only credited or replaced. Printable copy gives the client's version. Issuing sends nothing.

15Record the money when it arrives

DoOn the invoice, under Money in, type what actually arrived, the day, and how. Click Record this payment. Part payments are fine — record what came in, not what was due.

CorrectPaid to date and Still outstanding both recompute from the ledger.

CarefulIf more arrives than was billed, Still outstanding shows 0.00 and says nothing about the excess. The overpayment appears on Today and on the client's printed copy — look there, not here.

16Read Today, every morning

DoClick Today. Work the list top down. Not now hides a row for this session only.

CorrectThree groups — Overdue, This week, Coming up — each row naming the client, what it is, and the one action. Overpayments, likely extensions and missed deadlines all surface here.

Part B — The engagement browser — client-documents

17Start the engagement browser

DoFrom client-documents\ run:
python web.py
to open the real store, or point it somewhere safe to practise:
python web.py --store C:\path\to\a\scratch\folder --port 5071

CorrectIt prints the folder it is using before it starts. Read that line. The page shows your engagements and five buttons.

CarefulDo not use ports 5060 or 5061 — Chrome refuses them silently and the page will never load.

18Run the sitting

DoClick Start an interview and answer one question per screen. ← Back returns to the previous one.

CorrectA counter such as 3 of about 52, and a progress bar. Questions you leave blank are recorded as blank rather than guessed.

CarefulIf a page will not move on and shows no message, the answer was rejected — most often a tax year outside the allowed range. Change the value and try again.

19Check the record before you create it

DoAt the end you get Review — every question and its answer. Click Change on anything wrong, correct it, and click Save the change. Then click Create the engagement.

CorrectBlank answers are shown as left blank, not as a guess. After creating, the engagement gets its reference and a lifecycle bar: sitting done → pack built → sent → signed → billed → paid → closed.

CarefulA fee typed below a stated minimum is accepted here and quietly raised to the minimum on the estimate. Check the fee estimate afterwards against what you agreed.

20Read the fee estimate

DoScroll down the engagement to Fee estimate.

CorrectEach service and its amount, and a total that matches Estimate total higher up the page.

CarefulThis is the price the client is quoted. The desk's own invoice catalogue can produce a different figure for the same work — where they disagree, the estimate is the one the client agreed to.

21Build the signing pack

DoClick Build the signing pack, then Build the pack. It takes about a minute, because one of the checks opens every document in a browser to prove it is readable.

CorrectThe signing pack is built. 11 checks, nothing flagged — and it tells you if a check had nothing to look at. The documents are written to the engagement's pack folder, with their stylesheet beside them. If any check fails you get nothing rather than half a pack.

CarefulLeave both checkboxes unticked. “Also read the prose” crashes the build with a server error after the documents have rendered, and “Put the invoice in too” fails unless a bill has already been raised here.

22Look at the documents before they go

DoClick Documents on the engagement, then Look at it on any row.

CorrectEvery document the file can produce, and for the ones not ready, exactly what is still missing. The on-screen copy carries a red PREVIEW — NOT THE COPY THAT GOES TO THE CLIENT band; the PDFs in the pack folder do not.

CarefulThe PDFs are correct, but their internal title still reads “(template)”. Harmless to the content, visible in a PDF reader's title bar.

If a step does not match its picture, that is either a defect or an out-of-date procedure, and finding out which is the job. Note what you saw, and which step number, before carrying on.

Faults referred to in the Careful notes are recorded in full in docs/WALKTHROUGH-DEFECTS.md, which is written for whoever fixes them rather than for whoever does this job.
